contributions.statement: Budget an agent-written pre/post-condition spec step before test generation at about 38% more tokens (16% more per unique bug found), and expect its bug-finding gain to appear only with several attempts (significant at k>=4, not at k=1).
contributions.evidence: Table 4: 336.7M vs 243.9M tokens; 5.9M vs 5.1M per unique bug. Table 2: detect@1 +4.2pp p=0.31, detect@5 +9.8pp p=0.035 (12 vs 3 discordant bugs, uncorrected across k). Branch coverage +2.5pp p=0.003. Specs extracted from fixed code; single-file bugs in one monorepo.

contributions.statement: Have a human review agent-extracted specs for missing error-handling contracts and omitted methods before generating tests from them; bugs whose violated contract the spec captured were detected far more often (54.9% vs 19.4%).
contributions.evidence: §5.3.1 Fisher test over 450 runs; audit: pseudo-replication across 90 bugs and confounding by bug difficulty; contract coverage LLM-judged with the fix diff visible. The human review step itself was not tested.
relative_to: human review of specs in SDD (P19)

reason: Industrial same-model comparison that prices the spec step and shows where its modest benefit appears; the larger quality claims rest on a same-vendor LLM judge.
